conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode

candidates.name: ProfitTargetAsMultipleOfInitialRisk
candidates.quote: if there have been several 20-tick moves every day where a 10-tick protective stop would not have been hit, a trader might look to enter trends on pullbacks... The trader who carefully selects a setup has about a 60 percent chance of making 20 ticks while risking about 10 ticks.
candidates.description: Size the profit-taking limit order as a multiple of the trade's own initial protective-stop distance (typically 1:1 to 2:1 reward:risk -- e.g., risk 10 ticks to target 20).
candidates.book_order_type: profit-taking limit order at entry price plus a multiple of the initial risk

complexity.reason: needs the trade's *initial* risk distance captured once at entry and held fixed for the life of the trade, independent of any later stop-tightening rule

el_words_needed: InitialStopPrice (not yet in the register; must be captured once at entry and not overwritten by later stop-tightening)
notes: Similar in shape to the corpus's AtrProfitTarget (profit target as a multiple of a distance), but the distance here is the trade's own realized initial stop, not an N-bar ATR.

candidates.name: ScaleOutAtMultiplesOfInitialRisk
candidates.quote: it is reasonable to take about half of your position off after the market has gone your way for a distance equal to about twice the size of your original protective stop... take another quarter off at three times your original stop size, at six points, then let the last quarter run.
candidates.description: Scale out of a swing position in stages tied to multiples of the initial stop distance: roughly half the position at 2R profit, another quarter at 3R, and let the remainder run to a strong opposite signal or the session close.
candidates.book_order_type: staged profit-taking limit orders at 2R and 3R, remainder held with a trailing stop

complexity.reason: the engine models one all-or-nothing position; independently sized partial exits at multiple profit tiers are a multi-unit feature it does not support

notes: Recorded per the mining brief's instruction to keep scaling-out candidates even though the engine only models a single all-or-nothing position.
R30-01 is the all-or-nothing simplification of this same idea at a single tier.

candidates.name: AvoidCountertrendScalpInStrongTrend
candidates.quote: Once you believe there is a trend, you must accept that 80 percent of reversal attempts will fail and evolve into flags. This makes it almost impossible for most traders to enter countertrend trades on stops and consistently make a profit.
candidates.description: Do not take a countertrend scalp entry against a trend judged to be strong; the large majority of reversal attempts fail and become flags (continuations) instead.
candidates.pseudocode:
// research: 'strong trend' and 'reversal (countertrend) attempt' classification are not reduced to a bar-level test in this chapter
blockCountertrendEntry = strongTrendContext[0] && isCountertrendSignal[0];
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (blocks a countertrend entry signal from being taken)

complexity.reason: "strong trend" and "countertrend reversal attempt" have no stated bar-level test in this chapter; a design decision (e.g., an always-in-direction concept) is needed first

candidates.name: ExitOnWeakFollowThroughAfterLargeTrendBar
candidates.quote: Bulls will also look to take profits on any sign of strength, like at the close and just above a large bull trend bar, or at the close of the next bar or two, especially if it is a small bar or has a bear close.
candidates.description: After a large trend bar forms in the trade's favor, exit at (or within a bar or two of) that bar's close if the follow-through weakens -- the next bar is small relative to recent range, or it closes against the trade.
candidates.book_order_type: exit at the market, or a limit order just above the large trend bar's close

complexity.reason: needs an average-range-based 'large bar' classification (a simple window average) combined with a cross-bar follow-through comparison

el_words_needed: Average or AvgTrueRange for the range baseline
notes: This is also why, per the same passage, many large trend-bar breakouts are followed by small bars and fail -- the same test could equally be read as a breakout-failure signal (Entry) rather than a profit-taking (Exit) signal; recorded here as the profit-taking use since that is this chapter's framing.

candidates.name: TrailStopBelowPriorBarLow
candidates.quote: Traders will also have a stop order below the low of the prior bar, below the most recent higher low, or at breakeven.
candidates.description: A simple bar-by-bar trailing stop: keep the protective stop one tick below the prior completed bar's low while long (above the prior bar's high while short).
candidates.pseudocode: exitLongStop = ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && low[0] <= low[1] - stopOffsetTicks * tick;
candidates.book_order_type: protective sell stop one tick below the prior bar's low
notes: Distinct from R29-05 (swing-pivot based) and R29-07 (lowest since entry): this is a fixed one-bar-lag trail, the simplest of the three.

candidates.name: ExitNearPriorSwingHighOnMaturingRally
candidates.quote: as the trend matures and develops more two-sided trading, they will no longer buy on a stop above the most recent swing high. Instead, as the rally weakens, they will look to take some profits above that high, or even a little below.
candidates.description: Once a rally is judged to be maturing/weakening, take profits at or slightly below the most recent swing high rather than waiting for a breakout continuation.
candidates.book_order_type: profit-taking limit order at or slightly below the most recent swing high

complexity.reason: needs both swing-pivot detection for the price level and a 'maturing/weakening trend' context test this chapter does not define mechanically

candidates.name: FixedTickScalpBracket
candidates.quote: they might buy AAPL for a 100 cent scalp and risk 50 cents... their initial order might automatically generate both a protective sell stop order at 50 cents below their entry price and a sell limit order at 100 cents above their entry price.
candidates.description: A scalper's OCO bracket: a fixed-distance protective stop and a fixed-distance profit target placed simultaneously at entry.
candidates.pseudocode:
exitLongStop = ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && ctx.OpenPositionProfit() <= -stopDollars;
exitLongTarget = ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && ctx.OpenPositionProfit() >= targetDollars;
candidates.book_order_type: OCO bracket: fixed-distance protective stop and fixed-distance profit-taking limit order

complexity.reason: a fixed-dollar open-profit comparison on each side

candidates.likely_existing_rule: StopLoss and TakeProfit (or TakeProfitWithRatioStop if one parameter should drive both legs)
notes: Nearly identical to the corpus's existing StopLoss/TakeProfit pair, just framed in ticks/cents rather than a raw dollar amount; kept per the dedup-hint convention.

rejected.quote: If the trader's equation is still favorable but not as strong as it was, experienced traders will often either tighten their protective stops or exit with a smaller profits. If the trader's equation becomes marginal... If it becomes negative, they should exit immediately at the market.
rejected.reason: the trader's equation depends on a continuously re-estimated subjective probability of success with no stated bar-level test

rejected.quote: you must realize that very smart bulls have limit orders to buy at the low of that bar, and the odds are on their side.
rejected.reason: assumes knowledge of other traders' resting limit orders (the order book), data the engine cannot observe from OHLCV bars

rejected.quote: you should check your account after every entry and exit to make sure that your current position and orders are what you think they should be... Never assume that your broker's software will work as expected 100 percent of the time.
rejected.reason: operational/broker-reliability advice, not a market-data-based trading condition

chapter_summary: This chapter covers profit-taking logic: sizing a profit target as a multiple of the trade's own initial risk (R30-01), staged scaling out at 2R/3R (R30-02, research-grade for the multi-unit limitation), a fixed-tick OCO scalp bracket that is close to the corpus's existing StopLoss/TakeProfit pair (R30-07), and several more contextual profit-taking triggers (weak follow-through after a large trend bar, a simple prior-bar-low trail, and taking profits near a maturing rally's swing high) that lean on trend/pivot context this chapter does not itself define mechanically. It also reiterates that most traders should avoid countertrend scalps against a strong trend (R30-03, research-grade). Several passages (the trader's equation as a continuous decision rule, assumptions about other traders' resting orders, and broker-reliability checklisting) were rejected as non-mechanical or requiring data the engine cannot have.
